open_points.subject: REGISTRY_BASE_URL configuration lifecycle
open_points.text: A30 now says “REGISTRY_BASE_URL is read by the Registry gateway at each call, not at start-up: it is no required start-up variable,” while State 0 R0-10 says the service “is configured only by environment variables, which it validates when it starts,” and State 1 describes RuntimeSettings/RuntimeEnvironment as startup configuration read from the environment.
open_points.question: Must startup validation exclude REGISTRY_BASE_URL entirely, with its absence or invalidity detected only when a Registry call occurs, or must it still be captured and validated in startup RuntimeSettings?
options: Exclude REGISTRY_BASE_URL from startup RuntimeSettings and read and validate the current environment value on every Registry call.
Read REGISTRY_BASE_URL into RuntimeSettings and validate it at startup, despite A30’s new per-call rule.
Permit startup without the variable but capture it once if present, rather than rereading it on every call.
open_points.default_guess: Follow the changed A30 and A6: exclude REGISTRY_BASE_URL from startup validation and RuntimeSettings capture, and resolve it afresh for each Registry call.

witness.initial: The service is launched with REGISTRY_BASE_URL present but malformed or unusable; all other required startup variables are valid.
events: The deployment operator starts the service.
After startup, a caller invokes an operation requiring Registry validation.
outcomes: Following R0-10/startup RuntimeSettings literally, startup refuses the malformed Registry configuration and the service never becomes ready.
Following changed A30 and A6, startup succeeds; only the later Registry-dependent operation fails with RegistryFailureKind transport_error.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees whether the service starts, and the API caller sees whether a Registry-dependent request can be attempted.
